newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean government rejects labour law compromise.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean government rejects labour law compromise.

text.p: The chairman of South Korea's ruling New Korea Party on Wednesday ruled out compromise with militant union leaders who want a new labour law scrapped.

"We will not change the law," Lee Hong-koo told a news conference. But he added the government would try to correct "misunderstandings" by labour leaders about the legislation, which allows companies to lay off workers.
"The laws we have passed are the best solutions," Lee said, adding that workers had nothing to fear.
"The majority of the Korean people will support the measures we have taken. Come spring the majority of labour unions will see there will be neither a reduction of wages nor major layoffs."
Lee expressed optimism that the economy, suffering from high costs that have exacerbated a trade deficit, would pick up later this year.
"As we go into the second half, the economy will begin to show a recovery. People will see we have made a right decision," he said.
